oracle.source: Retained public CausalModel.identify_effect call on the declared bow-arc graph; all four standard estimands are absent. The product hedge certificate is a separate assertion.

reference_review.scope: Exact negative standard-strategy result for one bow-arc graph. DoWhy produces no backdoor, IV, front-door or general-adjustment estimand; the product separately returns NotIdentified with identify.hedge on the same graph.
reference_review.independence_basis: Repository-authored public black-box CausalModel.identify_effect calls import no Antecedent implementation or test helpers. Inputs are the declared graph and explicit observed variable names. Two dummy rows provide a schema only; no data values enter graph identification. The negative product assertion requires all four strategy failures and no estimand expression, rather than one generic refusal substring.
reference_review.historical_exposure: Original generation environment and harness were deleted; historical author exposure cannot be established. Current review inspected product assertions and official DoWhy public API documentation. No upstream implementation or test source was consulted or copied.
reference_review.redistribution: Only repository-authored harness, frozen graph/output and dependency lock are retained under MIT OR Apache-2.0. DoWhy and transitive packages remain isolated tooling; their sources/tests are not copied into the product or ordinary CI.
reference_review.limitations: Failure of four standard DoWhy strategies does not prove general nonidentifiability or validate a hedge certificate. The product certificate assertion and separate exact SCM/completeness controls are distinct evidence. No effect estimation, positivity, uncertainty or calibration is established. Product DOT preparation uses its own latent projection; the black-box generator does not.
